content: The CAGE questionnaire is a widely validated tool used to screen for alcoholism. It has been shown to be effective in identifying individuals with problematic drinking behaviors. For instance, one study demonstrated that a CAGE score of 2 or higher has a sensitivity of 93% and a specificity of 76% for detecting problem drinkers. However, it is important to note that the CAGE questionnaire is not designed to diagnose other substance use disorders, although modified versions of the tool are sometimes used for this purpose. The CAGE questionnaire derives its name from the four key questions it asks. These questions are specifically designed to screen for alcohol use problems. If a respondent answers yes to two or more of the questions, further investigation is recommended. The four questions are as follows: 1. Have you ever felt the need to Cut down on your drinking? 2. Have people ever Annoyed you by criticizing your drinking? 3. Have you ever felt Guilty about your drinking? 4. Have you ever felt you needed a drink first thing in the morning (an Eye-opener) to steady your nerves or to get rid of a hangover? Each of these questions targets a specific aspect of problematic alcohol use, and the tool is designed to be a quick and effective screening method for identifying individuals who may require further evaluation or intervention.
